### (3) What is the relationship between health risk concentrations and healthcare market supply?

#### (goal is to ultimately assess health care supply-side institutional capacities and possible gaps)

##### First pass: calculate correlations between environmental risk variables and health care services/infrastructure (particularly for data series identified as targeting “migrant” health) but others too

Data Required:

-   healthcare facilities $\checkmark$

-   immigrant health centers $\checkmark$

-   environmental risks $\checkmark$

-   health problems $\checkmark$

-   H2-A population $\checkmark$


Correlations may be less reliable because I cannot group by county because R won't have enough observations to work with. Also, the states have different sets of health facility data, where some states have more or less recorded types of facilities. I could remove those differing variables, but then the only facility type in common would be hospitals, and I don't want to limit the data so much. When calculating correlations, I separated data by state, then aggregated all the data sets after calculating the coefficients. Only one correlation with Total H2A Workers was found to be not significant: Critical Access Hospitals in South Dakota.


```{r}
source("C:/Users/natha/OneDrive/Documents/internship/workspace/Processing/Healthcare.R")
migrant_health_centers()
state_facility_load()
healthcare()
```


Correlations between the total number of H-2A workers and healthcare facilities.

```{r}
# correlating between number of H-2A workers and the given health facilities
stateFacilityCorrelations()
h2aPopulationCorrelations <- h2aPopulationCorrelations |> mutate(PValue = round(PValue, 3)) |> arrange(desc(Correlation))
kable(h2aPopulationCorrelations, longtable = TRUE, align =c("l", "l", "l", "c", "c", "c"))

# write.csv(h2aPopulationCorrelations, file = "h2aPopulationCorrelations.csv")
```


Correlations between environmental factors and healthcare facilities.

```{r}
weather_facility_load()
create_response_predictors()

colorado_corr <- healthFacility_envir_correlations(colorado_full, response, predictors) |> na.omit()
utah_corr <- healthFacility_envir_correlations(utah_full, response, predictors) |> na.omit()
wyoming_corr <- healthFacility_envir_correlations(wyoming_full, response, predictors) |> na.omit()
northDakota_corr <- healthFacility_envir_correlations(northDakota_full, response, predictors) |> na.omit()
southDakota_corr <- healthFacility_envir_correlations(southDakota_full, response, predictors) |> na.omit()
montana_corr <- healthFacility_envir_correlations(montana_full, response, predictors) |> na.omit()

```
```{r}
colorado_corr_filtered <- colorado_corr |> filter(Sig == TRUE)
knitr::kable(colorado_corr_filtered)
cat("Number of Correlations Not Statistically Signifcant: ", nrow(colorado_corr) - nrow(colorado_corr_filtered))
```
